Toykut Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volyn Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Jews of Neskhizh (Toykut's Yiddish name) are first mentioned in 1569; from the mid-18th century, the community was represented by the Shapira branch of the Hasidic dynasty. The population reached 814 (43.7 percent) by 1897, dropping by more than half by 1921, though the remaining 435 Jews still made up 92.7 percent of the town. By August 1942, 480 of an estimated 520 Jews had been shot, erasing the community. This cemetery, founded no later than 1800, was known as 'Okopyshche'; according to the memoirs of Yakiv Abramchuk, it was destroyed by local residents for building materials immediately after the town's 1945 liberation from the Nazis.
